name: 牡蠣ひよっこ商店 広島本店 (Kaki Hiyokko Shoten Hiroshima Honten)

claims.text: Menu includes fried oysters, oyster-and-root-vegetable tempura and oyster gratin; fried items share oil/breading typical of izakaya and no GF handling is documented.
Dishes such as oyster ponzu and pots rely on standard Japanese soy sauce/ponzu, which contain wheat; no wheat-free seasoning is documented.
Virtually all dishes are oyster- or seafood-based, so vegan diners cannot be reliably accommodated.

name: 牡蠣と肉の店 ‐IPPO‐ 薬研堀店 (Kaki to Niku no Mise -IPPO- Yagenbori-ten)

claims.text: Oyster and yakiton dishes are seasoned with standard Japanese soy sauce and tare, which contain wheat; no wheat-free seasoning is mentioned.
The entire menu is built around oysters and pork, with shared grills and fryers, so vegan separation is not provided.

name: かきと水晶焼き 空 (Kaki to Suishouyaki Ku)

claims.text: As a Hiroshima izakaya the menu relies on standard Japanese seasonings, which are wheat-based soy sauce and ponzu; no gluten-free soy sauce is mentioned.
Cooking surfaces and grills are shared across oysters, conger eel, beef, and pork, so plant-only items cannot be guaranteed free of animal contact.

name: かき船 かなわ (Kakibune Kanawa)

claims.text: The restaurant's oyster and seafood dishes use Japanese soy sauce, ponzu, and dashi-based seasonings, which standardly contain wheat; fried oysters are breaded in wheat flour. No gluten-free preparation is documented.
The entire menu is oyster- and seafood-centered with fish-based dashi; there is no documented vegan or vegetarian preparation.
Dishes are seasoned in the standard Japanese style with soy sauce, which contains wheat; no wheat-free soy sauce is mentioned.

name: かき小屋袋町 海平商店 (Kakigoya Fukuromachi Umihei Shoten)

claims.text: The menu centers on oysters and seafood served grilled, steamed, and as sashimi, conventionally accompanied by Japanese soy sauce, which contains wheat; no wheat-free soy sauce is mentioned.
Dishes are prepared on shared oyster grills and seafood stations, so any non-seafood item would carry a high risk of contact with shellfish and fish.
The house specialty is an oyster oil-preserve and the cafe also serves dairy-based cheesecake, so the kitchen routinely handles seafood and dairy; no separate vegan preparation is described.

Oyster dishes are dressed with standard Japanese seasonings and the menu includes fried (breaded) oysters and oyster rice, which typically rely on wheat-based soy sauce, flour, and dashi; no gluten-free preparation is documented.
Every dish is built around oysters (shellfish) cooked on a shared grill and fryer, so the kitchen is not suitable for vegan diners and there are no plant-only options.
